subject: Community Preservation Act Funding and Development Impact
overview: The Council addressed the impacts of residential development on public safety and school capacity, receiving a report from the Superintendent of Schools regarding enrollment trends. Members also debated the equity of the Community Preservation Act's state matching funds and approved several infrastructure improvements for pedestrians and traffic safety.

items.title: Development Impact on Public Safety
items.summary: Referred to the Mayor a resolution to evaluate how recent and future residential development is affecting public safety personnel and whether expansion of staffing or facilities is required.

items.title: School Enrollment and Class Size Report
items.summary: Placed on file a report from the Superintendent indicating that while enrollment increased in September, recent residential developments have not yet significantly impacted student numbers or class sizes. The Council requested an updated report for mid-October.

items.title: Rental Unit Student Data and Chapter 40R
items.summary: Approved a request for data on students residing in rental units and amended it to have the Office of Community Development analyze Chapter 40R to maximize state reimbursements for affordable housing.

items.title: Future School Capacity Planning
items.summary: Approved a resolution calling for the creation of a 10-year plan to ensure schools are not overburdened by projected population increases.

items.title: Community Preservation Act State Match
items.summary: Approved a letter to the state delegation requesting full funding for the Community Preservation Act (CPA) state match after a petitioner argued the current 14.5% match is inequitable to local taxpayers. A motion to refer the matter to a subcommittee for a deeper review of local CPA options failed.

items.title: Willis Avenue Parking Restrictions
items.summary: Approved no-parking restrictions on the odd-numbered side of Willis Avenue between Rice and Willard Avenues to ensure emergency vehicle access on the narrow thoroughfare.

items.title: Mystic Valley Parkway Walkway Repairs
items.summary: Requested that the Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) and the state delegation coordinate repairs and lighting for the public walkway near 3920 Mystic Valley Parkway.

items.title: Medford Square Revitalization Scenarios
items.summary: Requested an update on administrative research into using specialized urban design firms to implement temporary revitalization scenarios like green spaces and bump-outs in Medford Square.

items.title: Recognition of Ball Square Cafe
items.summary: Congratulated the owner of Ball Square Cafe on being named 'Best Breakfast' by Boston A-List.

items.title: Development Committee and Mystic Ave Task Force
items.summary: Approved a request for the administration to appoint a development committee and a specific Mystic Avenue task force composed of residents to provide input on neighborhood-level impacts.

items.title: Public Safety Infrastructure Requests
items.summary: Approved requests to fill a pothole at the McGlynn School crosswalk and install crosswalk warning graphics at the South and Walnut Street intersection.

items.title: Election Warrant and Polling Locations
items.summary: Approved the warrant for the November 7 municipal election and requested that the Elections Commission review polling locations for more local options.

items.title: Highland Avenue Crosswalks and Eagle Scout Recognition
items.summary: Requested state action to paint crosswalks on Highland Avenue and noted future recognition for John Fee for his Eagle Scout project installing 100 hydrant markers.

items.title: Condon Shell Lighting for Farmers Market
items.summary: Requested that the Electrical Department activate lights at the Condon Shell during the final hours of the Farmers Market on Thursday afternoons.

items.title: Meeting Minutes
items.summary: Approved minutes from August 15, 2017, and tabled minutes from September 19, 2017.
